title: Prestressed weak-interface crack-to-supershear-to-spall mechanism ladder
purpose: Require independently observable crack-like, resolved supershear, and distributed spall-like responses before using AgentFEM for the JMPS 2025 weak-interface transition problem.
physics: near-incompressible finite-strain plane-stress Neo-Hookean strip with homogeneous preload, smooth remote impact, a fixed zero-thickness bilinear Mode-I interface, and a precrack

execution.evidence: The public benchmark runs three 30-facet cases through the same finite-strain Explicit lifecycle and reports preload transfer, acoustic-tensor bulk modes, crack-front fitting, distributed-failure timing, and the complete energy ledger. A short construction and integration smoke test remains in the default test suite.

observables: Threshold-interpolated crack position and a fit window spanning at least three interface cells at the prestrained shear-wave speed.
Unstretched reference Rayleigh speed and prestrained reference-coordinate shear and pressure bulk-wave speeds.
Per-increment simultaneous failure, failure accumulated within one specimen-thickness shear-wave time, and peak intact-ligament traction ratio.
Bulk, kinetic, cohesive recoverable, cohesive dissipated, prescribed-motion work, and relative energy-balance channels.
Preload interface opening, traction ratio, free-force release acceleration, and transfer energy jump.
acceptance: The release-only endpoint remains crack-like and below the declared reference Rayleigh boundary.
The impact endpoint has a fitted front above 1.05 c_s and below 0.95 c_d while fewer than ten percent of ligament facets fail in one increment.
The weak-interface endpoint fails at least eighty percent of the ligament within one thickness shear-wave time and is classified spall-like.
Every endpoint has relative energy-balance error at or below 0.5 percent and zero preload-transfer energy jump within 1e-12.
A fitted speed above c_d is never labelled supershear; it is either supported by distributed spall evidence or marked unresolved discrete failure.
limitations: This is a JMPS-inspired numerical mechanism benchmark, not curve-level reproduction of the publication's unpublished input deck or parameters.

The two-dimensional membrane uses local P33=0 condensation. Its homogeneous response now matches an affine thin-three-dimensional FEM patch, but a full thin-3D fracture counterpart and general near-incompressible locking control remain future gates.

The Rayleigh value remains the unstretched isotropic reference. The principal prestrained surface-wave solver correctly requires a traction-free base surface, whereas this weak interface carries normal preload before release.
The inexpensive mechanism ladder retains two cells through the height; the separate two-dimensional convergence contract uses 30x10 and 40x14 meshes with a lower non-spalling impact.

A two-rank sparse-payload cohesive assembler now closes physical ownership, node-wise serial equivalence, force, energy, and cross-rank-count restart contracts. Large-interface MPI profiling and a distributed V4 convergence study remain required before performance or publication claims.

quantities.name: shear_speed_ratios
quantities.description: Crack-like, resolved-supershear, and spall-like apparent-front speed ratios; the last value is deliberately not interpreted as a crack speed.

quantities.name: rapid_failed_fractions
quantities.description: Fractions of the intact ligament failing within one thickness shear-wave time.

quantities.name: relative_energy_errors
quantities.description: Final complete-ledger relative energy errors for the three mechanism endpoints.
